doc.title: Milt Fillius interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 18, 2000

title: Military service and the draft
summary: He thinks a short universal draft would be good for citizens and notes the Marines are fully staffed.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That’s hard, and as you said, you can’t help but become a stronger, better person for going through that.
That’s right. Well just going through boot camp, today you don’t have to go to war. If you can handle boot camp, say a Marine boot camp, you’re a better man, and you’re a better citizen too.
Do you think that a draft should still exist today?

Yeah, I do. I think it’s a mistake to lower the standards of the people in the service. I would make it an easy draft, I’d say take you in for a year, year and a half and then you’d go about your business as I guess the Swiss do that, and some other people. I wouldn’t draft them for four or five years and so on, but I think number one, I think everybody should do it. I think it’s worthwhile. I think it’s a good experience and it’s good for you to do that. But the things they’re doing now trouble me. They can’t fill — they’re sixty thousand people short. But the interesting thing is that the only service that is full is the Marines, and they’re the toughies. You go in there, you get hell. I mean that’s the worst. But they have every billet filled by volunteers. So I don’t know what that tells you but—
